cues.text: Each point on this line is the price of Bitcoin at the end of one hour: the close.
Joined together, the hourly closes show where price has been.
The same hours drawn as candles. A candle shows where price went during its hour, not only where it ended.
Open: the price when the hour began
Close: the price when the hour ended
The body of a candle runs from its open to its close. Green closed higher than it opened; red closed lower.
High: the top of the wick
Low: the bottom of the wick
The wicks reach the highest and lowest prices traded during the hour.
From here the chart keeps both. Market structure is read from the closes; the candles stay for detail.
We can plot the positions every time we create a new high. We label these positions as a Higher Highs (HH).
And also plot the positions where we make a new low between each HH. We label these positions as a Higher Lows (HL).
When we plot between the HH and HL positions we see a less noisy sawtooth gradually increasing on a lower-resolution plot.
Sometimes we don't a dip where the low is not increasing. This cannot be called a Higher Low. They are called Lower Lows (LL).
We will come back to LL later.
We can see from the sawtooth we are trending upwards.
Even though it may dip, it it keeps returning to the previous high and beyond. We can note the position where this happens.
Where this happens we call it a Break of Structure (BoS).
This may coincide with a HH
Or not.
The swing is range of prices between the HH and the BoS.
An Upswing is a swing that trends upwards.
It is characterised by a downleg from the HH to the LL, followed by an upleg from the LL to the BoS.
